task_description:
# SvelteKit i18n Lang Switcher with `hooks.server.js` and `transformPageChunk`

## Background
Build a small SvelteKit application that supports three UI locales (`en`, `de`, `fr`) and exposes a language switcher. The user's chosen locale must persist across page reloads via a cookie, and the server must rewrite the root `<html>` element so its `lang` attribute reflects the active locale — exactly the kind of `app.html` rewrite that is normally tricky to get right in SvelteKit. The rewrite must be performed inside `src/hooks.server.{js,ts}` using the `transformPageChunk` option of `resolve` (see https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/hooks#Server-hooks-handle), not inside the page component, so the correct `lang` attribute is already present on the initial server-rendered HTML.

The page must use Svelte 5 runes (`$props`, `$state`, or `$derived`) and SvelteKit form actions (with progressive enhancement via `use:enhance`) for the locale switch — the app must work with JavaScript disabled too.

Supported locales and greetings:
- `en` → "Hello, world!"
- `de` → "Hallo, Welt!"
- `fr` → "Bonjour, le monde !"

The default locale (when no cookie is set or the cookie value is invalid) is `en`.

## Requirements
- A SvelteKit project that builds and runs with **`@sveltejs/adapter-node`**.
- Routes:
  - `GET /` — renders a page showing:
    - The greeting for the current locale (the exact strings above).
    - The current locale code in an element with `data-testid="current-locale"` (text content is the locale code, e.g. `en`).
    - Three locale buttons inside an HTML `<form method="POST">` that switches to the selected locale. The buttons must be `<button type="submit" name="locale" value="en|de|fr">...</button>`, each with `data-testid="locale-btn-<code>"`.
  - The form on `/` must POST to a SvelteKit form action that sets the `locale` cookie to the submitted value and redirects (HTTP 303) back to `/`.
- `hooks.server.{js,ts}` must:
  - Read the `locale` cookie from the incoming request, validate it against the allowed set (`en`, `de`, `fr`), and fall back to `en` if missing or invalid.
  - Populate `event.locals.locale` with the resolved locale so server `load` functions can read it.
  - Use `resolve(event, { transformPageChunk })` to rewrite the `lang` attribute of the `<html>` element so the server-rendered HTML contains `<html lang="<locale>">`.
- The root `+layout.server.{js,ts}` (or equivalent server load) must expose the resolved locale (e.g. as `data.locale`) to the page component.
- Svelte 5: the `/` page (`+page.svelte`) must use at least one Svelte 5 rune (`$props`, `$state`, or `$derived`).
- Progressive enhancement: the locale switch form must use `use:enhance` from `$app/forms` **and** also work without JavaScript (i.e. plain `<form method="POST">` with a valid form action).
- The application must listen on port 3000 when started with the production build.

## Implementation Hints
- Scaffold with `npx sv create` and pick Svelte 5 + the Node adapter, or add `@sveltejs/adapter-node` manually and run `svelte-kit sync` so the build works.
- In `src/app.html`, leave the default `<html lang="en">` opening tag and rewrite it inside `transformPageChunk` using a string replace; the `event.locals.locale` set by `handle` is the source of truth.
- Store the chosen locale in a (non-HTTP-only is fine) `locale` cookie via `event.cookies.set('locale', value, { path: '/' })` from inside the form action.
- Use `redirect(303, '/')` from `@sveltejs/kit` after setting the cookie so the next render picks up the new locale.
- Keep the translations table in a small module (e.g. `src/lib/i18n.{js,ts}`) so the same dictionary can be reused from server and client code.
- Define `App.Locals` in `src/app.d.ts` (if using TypeScript) so `event.locals.locale` is typed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Project path: /home/user/sveltekit-i18n
- Start command: `npm run build && node build`
- Port: 3000 (the server must listen on port 3000; the verifier sets `PORT=3000` and `HOST=0.0.0.0`)
- Routes (accessible at `http://localhost:3000`):
  - `GET /`:
    - Returns HTTP 200.
    - The response HTML contains a root `<html>` element whose `lang` attribute equals the resolved locale (`en` by default).
    - The page contains the greeting text corresponding to the resolved locale (one of the three exact greetings listed above).
    - The page contains an element with `data-testid="current-locale"` whose visible text is the resolved locale code.
    - The page contains three submit buttons with `data-testid` values `locale-btn-en`, `locale-btn-de`, and `locale-btn-fr` inside a `<form method="POST">` that posts to `/` (the default form action of the page is acceptable).
  - Submitting the locale switch form:
    - POSTing the form (i.e. `name="locale"` set to one of `en|de|fr`) updates the `locale` cookie on the response and returns an HTTP 303 redirect whose `Location` header is `/`.
    - The subsequent `GET /` (sending back the `locale` cookie) reflects the new locale in both the `<html lang="...">` attribute and the greeting text.
- Server-side rendering:
  - The `<html lang>` attribute must be set on the initial HTML returned by the server (i.e. it must be observable from a plain `curl` of `/`, with no JavaScript execution).
- Cookies:
  - The locale must be persisted via a cookie named `locale`. Setting an unknown value in the cookie (e.g. `xx`) must cause the page to fall back to the default locale `en` (and **not** crash).
- Progressive enhancement (source-level):
  - `src/routes/+page.svelte` must import `enhance` from `$app/forms` and apply it via `use:enhance` to the locale switch form.
  - There must be a `+page.server.{js,ts}` (or equivalent root server file) that exports an `actions` object handling the locale switch.
  - `src/hooks.server.{js,ts}` must exist and call `resolve(event, { transformPageChunk: ... })`.

truth:
# Verification Plan

## Setup
1. Remove any pre-existing cookie jar files used by the verifier (e.g. `if [ -f /tmp/cookies.txt ]; then rm /tmp/cookies.txt; fi`).
2. cd /home/user/sveltekit-i18n
3. Ensure dependencies are installed (`npm install` if `node_modules` is missing) and the production build exists (`npm run build`).
4. Start the app in the background using the start command (`PORT=3000 HOST=0.0.0.0 node build &`) and wait until `http://localhost:3000/` returns HTTP 200.

## Verification Steps

1. **Default locale (no cookie)**
   - Request: `curl -s -i http://localhost:3000/` (no cookies sent).
   - Expected:
     - Status: `200`.
     - Body contains a root `<html ... lang="en"` opening tag (i.e. the `lang` attribute equals `en`).
     - Body contains the exact string `Hello, world!`.
     - Body contains an element with `data-testid="current-locale"` whose text content is `en`.
     - Body contains three buttons with `data-testid` values `locale-btn-en`, `locale-btn-de`, `locale-btn-fr` inside a `<form` element with `method="POST"`.

2. **Switch to German via the form action**
   - Request: `curl -s -i -X POST -d 'locale=de' -c /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:3000/?/setLocale` (the form action is the default page action, so the equivalent POST `http://localhost:3000/` is also acceptable).
   - Expected:
     - Status: 303 redirect with `Location: /`.
     - The response sets a `locale=de` cookie (visible in `Set-Cookie` header or in the saved cookie jar).
   - Follow-up request: `curl -s -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:3000/`.
   - Expected:
     - Body contains a root `<html ... lang="de"` opening tag.
     - Body contains the exact string `Hallo, Welt!`.
     - Element with `data-testid="current-locale"` has text `de`.

3. **Switch to French via the form action**
   - Request: `curl -s -i -X POST -d 'locale=fr' -b /tmp/cookies.txt -c /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:3000/`.
   - Expected:
     - Status: 303 redirect with `Location: /`.
     - The response sets a `locale=fr` cookie.
   - Follow-up: `curl -s -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:3000/`.
   - Expected:
     - Body contains a root `<html ... lang="fr"` opening tag.
     - Body contains the exact string `Bonjour, le monde !`.
     - Element with `data-testid="current-locale"` has text `fr`.

4. **Invalid locale cookie falls back to default**
   - Request: `curl -s --cookie 'locale=xx' http://localhost:3000/`.
   - Expected:
     - Status `200` (no crash, no 500).
     - Body contains a root `<html ... lang="en"` opening tag.
     - Body contains the exact string `Hello, world!`.

5. **Browser verification (Playwright via the `chromium` package)**
   - Browser verification: Launch a headless Chromium browser, navigate to `http://localhost:3000/`, and verify that:
     - `document.documentElement.lang === 'en'` and the visible page contains the text `Hello, world!`.
     - Clicking the button with `data-testid="locale-btn-de"` results in a navigation where `document.documentElement.lang === 'de'` and the page contains `Hallo, Welt!`.
     - Clicking the button with `data-testid="locale-btn-fr"` results in a navigation where `document.documentElement.lang === 'fr'` and the page contains `Bonjour, le monde !`.
     - Reloading the page after switching keeps the most recently selected locale (i.e. the cookie persists).

6. **Source-level checks**
   - The file `src/hooks.server.js` or `src/hooks.server.ts` exists under `/home/user/sveltekit-i18n/` and contains a call to `transformPageChunk`.
   - The file `src/routes/+page.svelte` exists and contains a `use:enhance` directive and an import from `$app/forms`.
   - A `+page.server.js` or `+page.server.ts` file at `src/routes/` exports an `actions` object.
   - The Node adapter is configured: `svelte.config.{js,ts}` references `@sveltejs/adapter-node`, and a `build/` directory exists after `npm run build`.
